questoes.enunciado: The cells indicated by the arrows are examples of:

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This cell is a mucus-secreting goblet cell, which is located in the lining epithelium of the small intestine. Mucus is a glycoprotein which can stain with either hematoxylin (as shown here) or eosin, depending on the composition of the mucus. Mucigen in these cells often appears vacuolated.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the glands indicated by the rectangles according to their shape.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These simple tubular glands form unbranched, cylindrical invaginations of the lining of the large intestine. These glands contain both absorptive cells and mucus-secreting goblet cells.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the gland that fills the field according to its structure.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Visible in this field are several sections of ducts, indicating a highly branching duct system; therefore, this is a compound gland. Furthermore, both serous-secreting acini and mucus-secreting tubules are visible.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the glands outlined in this image according to their structure.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Each sweat gland in the skin has a long, unbranched duct, which ends in the coiled secretory portion of the gland. In this section, the portions of the ducts that connect with the glands are not visible, as they pass out of the plane of section.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the gland that fills the field according to its structure.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Visible in this field are numerous sections of ducts indicating a highly branching duct system; therefore, this is a compound gland. Furthermore, only serous-secreting acini are visible.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the outlined structures in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Serous demilunes consist of a cap of serous-secreting cells at the end of a mucous tubule. The secretory products of these cells pass into the lumen of the tubule.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures circled in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Interlobular ducts, receiving the secretory products from multiple lobules, are located in the dense, irregular, interlobular connective tissue. These ducts often have a stratified cuboidal or stratified columnar epithelium.

questoes.enunciado: Name the mode of secretion of the cells that make up the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This acinus is composed of pyramidal-shaped cells with numerous distinct secretory granules. Their contents are released by the merocrine mode of secretion. During the process of secretion, the membrane of the granule fuses with the apical plasma membrane of the cell (exocytosis) and the granule contents only are released into the lumen of the acinus.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the gland indicated by the rectangle according to its structure.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These tubular glands of the stomach extend from an invagination from the surface epithelium which serves as the duct. The tubular secretory units branch from this single duct.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. A compound gland is subdivided into numerous lobules, which are connected by interlobular ducts. Intervening interlobular connective tissue separates the lobules.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure enclosed by the rectangle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Intralobular ducts are surrounded by the secretory parenchyma of the gland. In some cases, a small amount of loose, intralobular connective tissue is visible. These ducts are lined by an epithelium which ranges from low cuboidal to low columnar.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the gland that fills the field according to its structure.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This sebaceous gland is composed of acini that branch from the hair follicle that serves as the duct. The cells of the acinus produce a thick, oily secretion that accumulates in the cells. Secretion is by the holocrine mode as entire cells are shed with their secretory contents onto the hair shaft.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the gland that fills the field according to its structure.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This low magnification image shows a compound tubulo-acinar gland in which nearly all the secretory units are mucus-secreting tubules. The more darkly stained area in the upper left contains serous-secreting acini. Also visible are numerous ducts indicating a highly branching duct system; therefore, this is a compound gland.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the encircled structures in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The acinus is a spherical structure composed of pyramidal-shaped cells and forms the basic secretory unit of some glands. In this case, this acinus produces a serous product, as evidenced by the presence of distinct secretory granules, and the individual cells release their secretory product by the merocrine mode of section. Two pale-staining interlobular ducts are also visible.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the gland seen in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This is an example of a sheet gland which consists of an epithelium composed entirely of mucus-secreting goblet cells. The best example of a sheet gland is that which lines the stomach, seen here. The mucous secretions of these cells protect the stomach lining from the acidic contents.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CORRECT.  This cell is a mucus-secreting goblet cell, which is located in the lining epithelium of the small intestine.  Mucus is a glycoprotein which can stain with either hematoxylin (as shown here) or eosin, depending on the composition of the mucus.  Mucigen in these cells often appears vacuolated.
